summary: Implemented a dedicated Phase 1 runtime-logging seam with structured progress events, explicit stop records, and convergence-evidence capture on top of the existing runtime controller.
key_findings: `autofdtd.diagnostics.runtime_logging` now defines immutable `RuntimeLogEvent`, `RuntimeConvergenceSample`, `RuntimeConvergenceEvidence`, and `RuntimeExecutionLog` models plus `RuntimeProgressLogger` for deterministic progress emission and stop-summary capture.

`autofdtd.runtime.run_until_stop_with_logging()` now drives the existing stop-policy controller while returning a structured execution log instead of only the final stop decision, keeping logging separate from solver kernels and future benchmark metrics.

Convergence evidence is captured for every shutoff check even when progress logging is downsampled, so Phase 1 runs preserve both operator-facing progress records and the full check history needed to diagnose early-stop behavior.
Focused tests and examples cover shutoff-triggered runs, step-limit runs, JSONL event export, and the new runtime-logging handoff surface.

artifacts.description: Structured runtime logging models, JSONL export, convergence evidence capture, and the reusable progress logger.
Logged execution helper layered on the existing runtime controller.

Documentation describing the Phase 1 runtime-logging seam and its separation from benchmark metrics.

follow_up_notes: Verified with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests/test_runtime_controls.py tests/test_runtime_logging.py`, `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests/test_imports.py`, `PYTHONPATH=src python -m compileall src`, and a direct `runtime_logging_demo()` smoke run. `ruff` was not available in this environment. Later timestep-loop work should reuse `RuntimeProgressLogger` and `RuntimeExecutionLog` directly so full Maxwell runs and future throughput metrics share one structured progress format.
